newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-MILAN STRIKER COMPLAINS OF LACK OF GAMES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MILAN STRIKER COMPLAINS OF LACK OF GAMES.

text.p: Striker Christophe Dugarry is unhappy with the lack of first team soccer at AC Milan and fears it may jeopardise his chances of making France's 1998 World Cup squad.
"There's a 50 percent chance I'll leave Milan," Dugarry said after being included in France coach Aime Jacquet's squad for next week's friendly home international against the Netherlands.
"If I have to leave to play, then I 'll leave... When I signed my contract there were three of us for two places... now there are five," he told Friday's L'Equipe.
"For me the national team is everything."
He said he did not know where he might go to at the end of the season, should he leave Milan, but it would not be to an Italian club.
"After Milan, I couldn't go elsewhere (in Italy)."
Dugarry began the Italian leg of his career at a disadvantage after arriving in Milan with an injury he picked up during the European championship finals in England last June.
He was injured during France's quarter-final against the Netherlands in Liverpool and missed the semifinal, their last match, against the Czech Republic in Manchester.
He was recalled by Jacquet for last month's friendly in Portugal and helped France to an impressive 2-0 away victory.
